hypothesis: An exact identity-alphabet certificate can skip NFKC, NFKD and Mn stripping for ordinary non-ASCII strings containing only ASCII, unified Han and a small explicit set of normalization-stable punctuation. The existing tokenization and all fallback paths remain byte-for-byte equivalent in result. This targets repeated lexical analysis in token packing without a persistent cache.

eligibility.proof: Every admitted scalar is individually unchanged by NFKC and NFKD, is not Mn and has canonical combining class zero. The alphabet excludes Hangul Jamo and every combining mark, preventing cross-character composition/reordering. Camel separation and casefold remain applied and map this alphabet back into itself. The complete string must match; any other character uses the existing implementation.
eligibility.fallback: Unknown UCD version, subclass/nonordinary hooks, or any non-admitted scalar retain the historical normalization/deletion work. No Unicode table, global normalization behavior, indexed token, ranking, source span or response may change.

Mixed and boundary strings, actual source dates, identifiers, Chinese question phrases, accents, compatibility characters, Jamo, combining marks, surrogates and special tokens match the forced historical path exactly for query/index modes.
Real C-call profiling verifies eliminated normalizer/category work only on the admitted alphabet; unsupported inputs keep historical work.
Ordinary function and Unicode-version guards preserve monkeypatched and unknown-version fallback.
Source/index and full non-timing recall payloads remain equal on invented native/token/optional paths.
